notes: GR12 gives the means wholly to the implementor; it asks for a means of identifying a statement, not a value no other statement shares, and no line-number means is unique when two statements share a line (a case the reader already recorded). The compiler's means is the statement's line in the source file that holds it: copied statements report their library text's lines (1, 2), main text 18, 19, 21. GnuCOBOL's DEBUG-LINE is the same per-file statement line (from its code generator; not run here, no cobc), which settles the latitude under CLAUDE.md rule 1, ISO 2023 having no debugging module to control it. The behaviour conforms; the documentation does not yet say which file's line, a documentation gap rather than a wrong value. Attack point: a reading that 'a particular source statement' demands a value unique within the resultant program after COPY.

next.reason: 1985: "The content of DEBUG-LINE is the implementor-defined means of identifying a particular source statement."; 2023: "No candidate covers the Debug module or DEBUG-LINE; the 2023 USE statement rules cover only exception, file and report declaratives". No 2023 clause holds the Debug feature, and the 2023 USE rules have no FOR DEBUGGING form or DEBUG-LINE special register. The Debug module is dropped.
